title: Feedback that sends the student back
statement: Feedback on a wrong answer says where to look, never what the student has to produce, and only what is true of what they were given.
detail:
Code holds feedback that names the right answer or speaks of how a film is made ("the second frame"); the judge then
checks each line against what the film has said and shown by its stop, and against the text
(`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/util.js`, `stopChecks` and `feedbackJudged`). The checks exist because a finished block
had a line saying the film had said something it hadn't. Since then, drafts have been held for "the second frame" and
for feedback that named the answer, and the film check made again under these checks had all 9 lines confirmed
(`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, "Video essay and the unit-video modules"). A hint may point to the line to read, even
quote it, but copies no run of the answer (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/open-check.js`); where the line itself is the
answer, the hint names who speaks or what moment to look at, without quoting it
(`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/evidence-hunt.js`); a nearly exact quotation is told it is near, without the text's
wording (`g9/transformer/src/glue/animated-judge.js`). The film kit's rule is the same: feedback on a wrong option
says why it is wrong and points back to the scene without naming the right one
(`othello-unit-video/.claude/skills/uvk-checks-make/SKILL.md`).
against:
the key-words block's hint gives the word's
first letter (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/key-words.js`), and after the last try a 3D version's reply gives the
text's wording (`g9/transformer/src/glue/`). A later run found: a research summary on choice items says the minimum effective feedback is showing the correct answer, and that without feedback the wrong options can be learned as true (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0159-mcq-principles-blueprints.qmd`). A later run found: the prompts a reading QC pipeline runs pass feedback on a wrong option that states the correct answer outright, so that the student 'should leave knowing what the right answer is and why' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/external_submodules/reading-question-qc/qc_pipeline/config/prompts.json`). A later run found: a reading-question feedback rubric bundled with the AP work's evaluator requires feedback on a wrong choice to state the correct answer or clearly guide the student to it, so the student leaves knowing the right answer (`icloud-work/inceptbench/submodules/reading-question-qc/qc_pipeline/config/prompts.json`). A later run found: an AP lesson spec's corrective line for a link that is only chronology names example mechanisms the answer could use, which says what to produce rather than only where to look (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/apush/source/sealed-authoring/authoring/apush/canonical/unit2/lesson-01.json`). A later run found: research summarised in an MCQ guide that, to keep students from later giving the wrong options they saw as answers, the minimum effective feedback is showing the correct answer (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0159-mcq-principles-blueprints.qmd`). A later run found counter-evidence (`icloud-work/incept/inceptbench/src/inceptbench/prompts/mcq_set/evaluation.txt`). A later run found counter-evidence (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/external_submodules/reading-question-qc/qc_pipeline/config/prompts.json`). A later run found counter-evidence (`icloud-work/inceptbench/submodules/reading-question-qc/qc_pipeline/config/prompts.json`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/feedback_clean.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/instruction-quality-standard.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D1-gradual-release-explicit-instruction.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0081-g3-reviewer-feedback-raw-2026-07-02-reading-explorers-v2-review-verbatim.qmd`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Generic Instruction BrainLift.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Direct Instruction BrainLift.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`shadow-content-eval/SKILL.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/lesson_bundle/evaluation.txt`). The synthesis says the evidence is "Drawn from second-language classrooms, so applied here by analogy to early oral language.", and for growing a child's language in comprehension talk it still prefers recasts and follow-up questions over right-or-wrong marking. The research comes from second-language classrooms and is applied to early oral language by analogy (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/course-red-team/references/opportunities-to-respond-brainlift.md`). A later run found: the code check that holds feedback naming the answer needs at least three of the answer's words in a row, so it never flags a one- or two-word answer: on one film block, two wrong-option lines naming a two-word key passed while a three-word key in the next question was caught (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/util.js`). A later run found counter-evidence (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/key-words.js`).
